PORT the owner-approved design into the real Command Center Hive page (/command-center).
Source of truth: docs/design/reference/command-center-artifact/index.html (a slimmed copy of the owner's artifact: its inline CSS and its <script type=module> code; base64 images were removed and are described in the contract). LOOK at docs/design/reference/command-center-artifact/hive-desktop.png, hive-full.png and hive-phone.png (how the artifact renders) and at docs/design/reference/hive-target.png (the owner's bar). The result must look like the artifact screenshot: same layout, same CSS (port it rule by rule, scoped as the contract says), same canvas drawing and animations (port the drawing functions, keep their timing and look), same typography.
Bind everything to REAL data from the existing app: tools/watch-assets/command-center-data.js parses the snapshot from /api/command-center (built server-side by tools/command-center-snapshot.mjs from the board payload) and /api/command-center/project?id= (buildProjectCockpit). Where the artifact reads its static `D` object, read the equivalent live field. Never hard-code sample numbers; missing values render as a short muted line.
Read coordination/review/cc-design-contract.md first and follow it exactly (file ownership, stylesheet order, fonts, icons, robot heads, CSP: no inline scripts, hooks to keep, the Array.from rule).
Motion: keep the artifact's animations (canvas loops via requestAnimationFrame, CSS keyframes), pause when the tab is hidden, off under prefers-reduced-motion; keep its glitch limits (each burst under 400 ms, at most 3 at once, never on text being read).
Tests: the tests in your outputs assert the OLD markup; update them to the new markup but keep every data-behaviour assertion (which number comes from which field, empty states, navigation, data-project-id). Tests in context are read-only and must keep passing.
You cannot run a browser. Reason concretely about sizes at 1440x900 and 390x844. When done, summarize what you ported, what you could not bind to live data and why.
